subject: people in cave
title: What If You Lived With No Clocks or Daylight for 40 Days? 15 People Did

scenes.text: What if you had no clock, no sun, no phone for 40 days? Your days would stretch.
In 2021, 15 volunteers walked into the Lombrives cave in France. 10 degrees, 100 percent humidity, and no light but their own.
They slept when tired and ate when hungry. Sensors and a swallowed thermometer capsule tracked every body, around the clock they couldn't see.
Their days stretched to about 32 hours on average. One person's day ran to 42 hours.
When they came out after 40 days, most believed it had been about 30. One was sure it was 23.
scenes.keywords: people walking out of cave sunlight

scenes.text: Two thirds of them wanted to stay longer. Without the sun, your body doesn't lose time. It just makes its own.

description:
What if you lived with no clocks, no daylight and no contact with the outside world? In 2021, fifteen volunteers in the Deep Time project spent 40 days in the Lombrives cave in France at 10 degrees Celsius and 100 percent humidity.
With sensors tracking sleep, temperature and social contact, their subjective days stretched to about 32 hours on average, and one person's to about 42; most thought only 30 days had passed when they emerged, and one guessed 23. Two thirds wanted to stay longer.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: WHAT IF YOU LOST THE CLOCK?
first_comment: The project cost 1.2 million euros and ran 50 separate experiments at once. How long do you think you'd last down there, and what should we run through next?
